question:
What is the value of the following expression?

\[ \begin{gathered} \small (1901 + 1902 + 1903 + \cdots + 1993) \\ \small {}- (101 + 102 + 103 + \cdots + 193) \end{gathered} \]
solution:
The two sums have matching patterns: \(1901\) is \(1800\) more than \(101\), \(1902\) is \(1800\) more than \(102\), and this continues through the last terms. Pairing corresponding terms therefore avoids calculating either large sum separately.

There are \(193-101+1=93\) terms in each sum, including both endpoints. Subtracting the second sum removes each of its terms once, so the difference is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(1901-101)+\cdots+(1993-193)\\
&\qquad=93\times1800=167{,}400.
\end{aligned}
\]
The value is \(167{,}400\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
